newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: WAGES DATA KNOCK THE WIND OUT OF AUSTRALIAN DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: WAGES DATA KNOCK THE WIND OUT OF AUSTRALIAN DOLLAR.

text.p: The resurgent Australian dollar had the wind knocked out of its sails on Thursday by news that not only had wages risen by less than previously thought in the second quarter, but private sector wages actually fell.

Moderate wages growth has been one of the factors that has allowed the Resrve Bank to ease rates five times since July 1996, and the better than expected data meant it was too early to rule out another, traders and analysts said.
By 12.30 p.m. (0230 GMT) the dollar had retreated to US$0.7440/45, having reached a high of US$0.7483 ahead of the data, to be down from Wednesday's local close of US0.7453/58.
